messages:
Jordan (Partnerships): Heads-up: CoreWeave sent an updated commercial term that includes a 'convertible reserve' feature. Theyallow converting a portion of reserved commits into spot with a fee. I think we should model this option before our next procurement decision.
Alex R: can you paste the relevant numbers?
Jordan (Partnerships): Quick paste from their sheet: cw-a100-40g reserved $48k/mo, spot floor $32k/mo, conversion fee 4% on converted capacity, up to 20% convertible per quarter, 7d notice, min commit 12 months. link to sheet: https://drive.redwood.example/coreweave-terms-v2
CoreWeave Rep: Confirming details. Conversions are processed with 7 calendar days notice; billing pro-rates daily. If we request conversion and supply is constrained, we notify within 24h and either fulfil partially or provide marketplace alternatives / credits.
Maria P: For cost modeling: Nina, can you run scenarios for 0%, 10%, 20% conversion across a 12-month commit and include the 4% fee? Also include a sensitivity for partial fulfilment.
Nina - Finance: Yes. Iwill run three scenarios and include an assumption for 0/25/50% partial fulfilment when conversion is requested. Goal: show net per-token delta and impact to gross margin. I'll post results in this thread later today.
Kevin L: Operational ask: if conversion moves us to spot, what's the observed preemption rate historically? We need to quantify the application-level cost to recover from preempts (restarts, cache warm-ups). CoreWeave, can you share anonymized stats?
CoreWeave Rep: Typical monthly preempt rates for these SKUs are 3-6%, with occasional spikes in high-demand windows. We'll add an appendix to the sheet with anonymized aggregates.
Alex R: Also: can the vendor map SKU -> region? If conversion forces us to fallback to marketplace SKUs in different regions, network latency and egress costs could change effective unit cost.
CoreWeave Rep: We'll add region tags to the SKU list and a regional availability column.
Jordan (Partnerships): Operational request from eng: include SRE contact on the procurement call to probe partial-fulfilment behavior and notification latency.
Kevin L: I'll join the call and bring a short list of questions about failover behavior. Also suggest we assume a 1.5x operational overhead to replace preempted capacity when modeling.
Nina - Finance: Preliminary note: the 4% conversion fee is applied to the dollar value of the capacity converted in that billing period; itdoes not compound. If conversion reduces our average monthly realized cost by >2% after factoring in replacement overhead and credits, it's worth pursuing.
Jordan (Partnerships): I'm going to propose a 30-day pilot where we test converting 10% once, with conversion fee capped at 2% for the pilot. That will let us validate preempt and partial-fulfilment assumptions.
CoreWeave Rep: Open to a pilot, can escalate. We'll need a short SOW and exact SKUs defined.
Alex R: Good. Action items: Nina runs the scenario table (0/10/20% convert + partial fulfilment buckets), Kevin adds preempt and latency impact, Jordan negotiates pilot + fee cap. I'll coordinate calendar invites.
VendorBot: New file uploaded: coreweave-terms-v2-appendix.csv
Maria P: One more ask: if we accept convertibility, can we negotiate a hard SLA around notification timelines (24h) and credit calculations? Important for risk modeling.
CoreWeave Rep: Will check with legal and circle back; notification and credit terms are negotiable for pilots.
Nina - Finance: I'll post the scenario CSV here once complete: https://drive.redwood.example/cost-scenarios-coreweave-1942201234.csv
Jordan (Partnerships): Thanks all. We'll reconvene after Nina posts the scenarios and then book a negotiation call with vendor SRE and commercial. :phone: :thumbsup:
Kevin L: thumbs up
Maria P: thanks everyone
